To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the calcareous plankton and isotopic proxies from ODP Site 1209 (Shatsky rise, Pacific Ocean) provide a high resolution record of the glacial–interglacial variability in the carbonate dissolution and paleoproductiveity in the mid-latitudinal NW Pacific over the past 450 ka.

1) the NDI proposed by Marino et al. (2009), is the most reliable dissolution index to be used for the study of calcareous plankton assemblages in the Pacific Ocean; 2) the dissolution of calcareous microfossils is primarily controlled by changes in the ocean carbonate ion concentration, rather than by variations in the organic flux; 3) the productivity changes over the last 250 ka were controlled by the northward migration/extension
the NDI data from Site 1209 represent evidence of preservation minima during glacial phases, whereas dissolution peaks were recorded at the onset or during interglacial phases.
In summary, our research is concerned with

a high-resolution multi-proxy study of calcareous plankton and isotopes from Shatsky rise (ODP Site U1209B, Northwest Pacific Ocean) to interpret the calcite dissolution and the paleoproductivity fluctuations of the last 400 ka.
the potential of calcite dissolution and productivity proxies to evaluate paleoceanographic and climate changes over the last 400 ka.
the potential of calcite dissolution and nannofossil paleoproductivity records as proxies for the reconstruction of paleoenvironmental conditions in the NW Pacific.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the changes in carbonate preservation and calcareous plankton assemblages at Site 1209 are controlled by both the ocean chemistry (carbon chemistry) and the productivity changes.

the changes in calcite preservation and paleoproductivities at Site 1209 are primarily driven by the changes in the oceanic carbonate ion concentration (related to the changes in the carbonate ion concentration) and the thermocline depth (controlled by the changes in wind stress and/or the strength of the Kuro-Shio Extension).

both the dissolution and paleoproductive indices are strongly influenced by the glacial/interstadial variability, whereas the obliquity-driven changes in paleoproductivities are mainly related to the changes of the thermoclinic/nutriclinic depth.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
calcareous nanno- and planktonic microfossils from Site 1209 can be used to evaluate the paleoproductivity variations and the dissolution intensity over the last 500 ka.

calcareous nanno-fossils can be a reliable proxy for reconstructing paleoenvironmental changes at mid-latitudes, but the choice of dissolution indices and the selection of the most appropriate nannofossil species are essential for the proper interpretation of the paleoenvironmental data.

the NDI is a good dissolution indicator, particularly at sites located at the upper part of the calcite lysocline and that the changes in the calcite preservation are controlled by the changes in the ocean carbonate chemistry rather than the variations of the organic carbon flux at our site.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the nannofossil preservation and assemblages are sensitive to both ocean chemistry and productivity, and that the latter can be used as a paleoceanographic indicator of the thermoclinic and nutriclinic dynamics.

the high-resolution, multi-proxied dataset from ODP Site 1209 is a powerful archive to study the ocean chemistry and productivity changes in the Pacific Ocean during the last glacial–intergalcial cycles.
the high-resolution, multi-proxied dataset from Site 1209 is an excellent archive of the oceanographic and climate variability over the last 0.5 Ma.
